children: BlackBerry raised its full-year targets outlook after posting higher earnings and revenue for the second quarter, boosted by strong growth in its QNX embedded software business.

The Canadian cybersecurity and software company on Thursday upgraded its guidance for fiscal 2027. The company now expects total revenue to be in the range of $616 million to $636 million, with adjusted earnings per share in the range of 19 cents to 22 cents.
Previously, BlackBerry expected revenue of $594 million to $621 million, with adjusted earnings of 16 cents to 20 cents a share.
For its second quarter ended Aug. 31, BlackBerry posted net income of $33.9 million, or 5 cents a share, up from $13.3 million, or 2 cents a share in the comparable quarter a year ago.
Adjusted earnings were 7 cents a share. According to FactSet, analysts were expecting 4 cents a share, in line with company guidance.
Revenue rose 26% to $163.3 million from $129.6 million, topping its own guidance range of $137 million to $148 million, and analyst forecasts of $142.5 million.
The company benefited from a strong performance from its embedded software segment, QNX, which saw a 27% increase in revenue to $80.3 million.
BlackBerry's Secure Communication unit logged a 2% increase in revenue to $60.9 million.

Looking ahead to the third quarter, the company expects revenue in the range of $143 million to $154 million, with QNX contributing between $82 million and $88 million, and Secure Communication $55 million to $60 million.
